clue.text: Idling lout tucked into fish

indicators.note: the lout is tucked into the fish, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: a ling is a long sea fish of the cod family
an oaf is a clumsy, boorish lout

explanation.surface: A lazy lout lounges about, stuffed full of fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Lazing around doing nothing is idle behaviour, the same sense as idling.

clue.text: Free from Braille

indicators.note: the answer is made from the letters of the next word, rearranged

explanation.surface: Something is released from a blind reader's raised-dot script.
explanation.definitionFit: Liberal means generous or not strict, so free with something or freely given.

clue.text: Address car with a poem

parts.note: a tar is a sailor, abbreviated AB for able seaman
an ode is a lyric poem

explanation.surface: A sailor addresses someone in verse.
explanation.walkthrough: AB stands for able-bodied seaman, a crossword staple for a sailor or tar.
explanation.definitionFit: One's address is where one lives, one's home or dwelling.

clue.text: Country shown in diagrams

indicators.note: the letters are on show in the words that follow, run across the word break

explanation.surface: A nation is depicted on charts.
explanation.definitionFit: India is a large nation in South Asia.

clue.text: Putting shining element on hair dye is hell!

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece put on another sits above it, so it comes first

parts.note: Ge is the chemical symbol for germanium, a lustrous grey metalloid
henna is a reddish dye used on hair

explanation.surface: Applying a glittering chemical on top of tinted hair is a nightmare.
explanation.walkthrough: Gehenna is a biblical name for hell, from a valley outside Jerusalem.
explanation.definitionFit: In Jewish and Christian scripture it is the place of torment for the wicked, the underworld of punishment.

clue.text: The discussion group remains in uproar

indicators.note: a word thrown into uproar has its letters thrown into disorder and rearranged

explanation.surface: A debating society is still arguing noisily.
explanation.definitionFit: A seminar is a small class of students meeting to discuss a topic with a tutor.

clue.text: Persuaded top player to take foreign nobleman

indicators.note: the top player takes in the nobleman, holding him inside

parts.note: a seed is a top-ranked player in a tennis tournament
duc is French for duke

explanation.surface: A star player was coaxed into hosting a visiting aristocrat.
explanation.definitionFit: To seduce is to lead astray or win over, so a person seduced has been tempted into something.

clue.text: Storm out after a terrible meal in a whirl

indicators.note: one piece comes after the other in the answer
a terrible dish is a mess, so these letters are jumbled
something out of order is disordered, so these letters are rearranged too

explanation.surface: A diner storms out after a dreadful dinner, head spinning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Storm' looks like the start of the definition but is anagram fodder signalled by 'out'; 'terrible' jumbles MEAL to MAEL, and 'after' sets the stormy part second.
explanation.definitionFit: A maelstrom is a powerful whirlpool, a swirling vortex of water.

clue.text: Hurried back to the allotment with the story

indicators.note: back means the word for hurried is read in reverse

parts.note: ran means hurried
a ration is a fixed allotment of food or supplies

explanation.surface: A gardener rushed back to the vegetable plot with a tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns RAN into NAR. 'allotment' looks like a British garden plot but means a share.
explanation.definitionFit: Narration is the telling of a tale, the account a narrator gives.

clue.text: Rest of the uncoordinated team were in a French street

indicators.note: the jumbled team goes in the street, inside it

parts.note: rue is French for street

indicators.note: an uncoordinated group is in disarray, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: a side is a sports team

explanation.surface: The rest of a clumsy football team ended up in a Paris road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uncoordinated' jumbles the team (SIDE) to ESID; 'Rest' looks like a verb but is the noun, what is left over.
explanation.definitionFit: A residue is what remains, the leftover part.

clue.text: Slaughter in the theatre!

parts.note: read as a stage tragedy full of killing, but it also hints at the blood spilt in an operating theatre

explanation.surface: A gory play leaves the stage strewn with bodies.
explanation.definitionFit: Massacre and killing on a large scale is called by a word built from spilt blood.

clue.text: Organs which take money to buy titles

indicators.note: the organs take in the money, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: ears are the organs of hearing
L stands for pound, the British unit of money, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Bodies that accept cash in exchange for honours, a cash-for-peerages scandal.
explanation.definitionFit: Earl is a rank in the British peerage, a hereditary noble title.

clue.text: Agitated manner I show mathematician

indicators.note: something agitated is shaken up, so these letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: I show a nervous manner in front of a maths professor.
explanation.definitionFit: Bernhard Riemann was a nineteenth-century German mathematician famed for his geometry and hypothesis.

clue.text: Copper's not quite too late for the sauce

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper, and the 's adds an S

indicators.note: not quite the whole word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: tardy means slow or too late

explanation.surface: A policeman arrives a little late for the gravy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a policeman but is the metal, symbol Cu. 'not quite' trims the Y from TARDY to leave TARD.
explanation.definitionFit: Custard is a sweet yellow pouring sauce served over puddings in Britain.

clue.text: Figure lad could be in Baywatch?

definitions.text: Figure lad could be in Baywatch?

indicators.note: these letters could be rearranged into another word, signalling an anagram

explanation.surface: A muscular young man might find himself cast in the beach television drama.
explanation.walkthrough: Baywatch was an American TV series about beach rescuers on the California coast, so the whole clue describes the answer as well as building it.
explanation.definitionFit: Baywatch followed the beach rescue staff who watch swimmers and save them from drowning.

clue.text: Remitting in favour of making a donation

parts.note: for means in support of
giving is making a donation

explanation.surface: A charity pardons debts in favour of receiving gifts.
explanation.definitionFit: Remitting a debt or sin means pardoning or letting it off, an act of mercy.

clue.text: Grouse when gang leader made ribs sore

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter
sore here means upset or troubled, so the letters are in a troubled order

explanation.surface: A complaint arises when the gang boss leaves a victim's ribs aching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grouse' wants to be a verb, complain, but it is the bird shot for sport.
explanation.definitionFit: Grouse are an example of birds shot for sport on moors in season.

clue.text: Get up about midday to get a lift

indicators.note: the word for getting up goes about, around, the other letter

parts.note: to rise is to get up out of bed
read as mid-day: the middle letter of the word day is A

explanation.surface: Someone sleeps in till noon before hitching a ride.
explanation.walkthrough: 'midday' looks like noon, but split as mid-day it gives the central letter of DAY.
explanation.definitionFit: A pay rise is called a raise; to raise something is to lift it.

clue.text: Meeting of very odd group

annotationWithheld.why: Meeting of very odd group (5) for FORUM: RUM can be 'very odd' but nothing in 'of' or 'group' gives FO or a container, so the clue as held looks misread or garbled and no search found the printed text

clue.text: Supply vessel contained fish? No, the opposite

indicators.note: one word is held inside the other
this reverses the stated order, so the fish holds the vessel instead

parts.note: an urn is a vase or vessel

explanation.surface: A container holding fish is supplied, or rather the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No, the opposite' tells the solver to swap container and contents from what 'contained' first suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: To furnish someone with something is to provide it.

clue.text: Bits cut off or added on!

definitions.meaning: the pieces snipped away when a hedge or hair is tidied
the decorations and extras added to a garment or a roast dinner

explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both the offcuts from a haircut and the garnishes or accompaniments to a meal, opposite senses.

clue.text: The girl took a long time to find a mosaic tile

parts.note: Tess is a girl's name
an era is a long period of time

explanation.surface: A girl takes ages hunting for a piece of mosaic.
explanation.definitionFit: A tessera is one of the small square pieces of stone or glass set into a mosaic.

clue.text: Put in clue to be solved by department head

indicators.note: a puzzle to be solved is worked out, so these letters are reworked
the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A setter puts in a clue for the head of department to crack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be solved' rearranges IN, CLUE and D, the first letter of department.
explanation.definitionFit: To include something is to put it in, to take it in as part of a whole.

clue.text: Hurried round with vase, but it wasn't acceptable

definitions.note: a past participle read as something that was not found acceptable

indicators.note: the word for hurried goes round the vase, enclosing it

parts.note: sped means hurried
an urn is a vase

explanation.surface: Someone rushed round with a vase, but the gift was rejected.
explanation.definitionFit: Something spurned has been rejected with contempt, turned down.

clue.text: Two forms of transport, or only one

parts.note: rail is travel by train, the first of the two modes
the bus is the second mode of road transport

explanation.surface: A traveller weighs taking two different services, or just a single one.
explanation.walkthrough: A railbus is a light bus-like vehicle that runs on railway lines, so it is two forms of transport combined in one.
explanation.definitionFit: The vehicle is a single conveyance combining a road coach body with rail wheels.

clue.text: Copper takes strong dislike to a grand house

indicators.note: the copper takes in the other pieces, holding them inside

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
hate is a strong dislike

explanation.surface: A policeman develops a loathing for a stately home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' again reads as a policeman but is the metal Cu, split around HATE and A.
explanation.definitionFit: A French country mansion or castle is a large stately residence.

clue.text: Make a collection at a service

parts.note: a mass is a church service

explanation.surface: Churchgoers pass a collection plate during worship.
explanation.definitionFit: To amass is to gather or accumulate a large quantity.

clue.text: Girl who made the list perhaps?

definitions.text: Girl who made the list perhaps?

parts.words: Girl who made the list perhaps?
parts.note: a girl's name hinted at by a famous political list named after a woman

explanation.surface: A young woman was chosen for the shortlist.
explanation.walkthrough: EMILY's List is a political organisation that backs women candidates, so a girl of that name might be said to have made the list.
explanation.definitionFit: Emily is a common girl's name, and the women's campaign group is called EMILY's List.

clue.text: The Frenchman's here, faltering because it's much colder

parts.note: ici is French for here, the word a Frenchman uses
er is the hesitant sound of someone faltering in speech

explanation.surface: A hesitant visitor from France remarks on how much chillier it has turned.
explanation.definitionFit: Something nearer to ice in temperature is colder, the comparative of icy.

clue.text: Cautioned about the teaching profession

indicators.note: the letters are moved about, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Teachers have been given a warning about their work.
explanation.definitionFit: Schooling as a field of work covers everyone who teaches, the sense of education as a sector.

clue.text: Drunk with water in large waves

parts.note: high can mean intoxicated, from drink or drugs
the sea is a body of water

explanation.surface: A drunk is thrown into the water among big breakers.
explanation.definitionFit: A high sea is a stormy ocean with tall swelling breakers, a sailor's phrase.

clue.text: Attempted to produce a composition for the editor

parts.note: an essay is a written composition
ed is the usual short form of editor

explanation.surface: A student tried to write a piece for the newspaper editor.
explanation.definitionFit: To essay something is an old-fashioned verb for trying it.
